items.entity: Volume fraction V_f of the Fig. 2 cantilever topology optimization
items.description: Fig. 2 contains three runs: (b) V_f=0.7, (c) 0.5 and (d) 0.3, so no single value defines 'the' example. For the same 150x52 cm cantilever, the Sec. 4.1 text gives V_f=0.5. This matches V=0.5*V_bar=3900 cm^3 (=0.5*150*52*1) and Figs. 4b/18b. The Fig. 12 caption for the same problem gives V_f=0.3.

items.entity: 100 kN point load at the free end, 18 cm below the top edge
items.description: Sec. 2.1 and 4.1 give only the magnitude and position; the direction appears only in Fig. 2a/12. Sec. 4.1 treats downward deflection as positive and reports a 3.88 mm deflection, which suggests a downward load. Table 3, however, has the top chord (members 1, 3, 5) in compression and the bottom chord in tension. For a cantilever clamped on the left, that implies an upward load or a vertically flipped image. Up vs. down gives the same compliance and density layout; a horizontal load would not.
readings: vertical downward (-y), transverse to the 150 cm span
vertical upward (+y): same compliance and density field as downward

items.description: Sec. 2.1 says mesh size changes the result but gives no mesh for the Fig. 2 runs. Only Sec. 4.1 (the Fig. 12 run) states 150 x 52 (x1) elements, i.e. 1 cm x 1 cm squares.

Sec. 1.3.1 says the domain is discretized with a 'structured grid and hexahedral linear elements'. Sec. 4.1 says '150 x 52 x 1 linear quadrilateral elements', and the 'x 1' suggests one layer through the thickness. Sec. 4.2 again says hexahedral.
readings: 3D 8-node linear hexahedra, one 1 cm layer through the thickness

items.entity: 2D stress state of the continuum model
items.description: Plane stress vs. plane strain is never stated (Sec. 1.3.1, 2.1, 4.1). 'Plate' and the 1 cm thickness suggest plane stress. Plane strain amounts to an effective E' = E/(1-nu^2) and nu' = nu/(1-nu), about 0.43.

items.entity: Out-of-plane thickness used in the TO finite-element model
items.description: Sec. 2.1 and 4.1 give a 1 cm thickness only 'for size optimization'. The thickness used for stiffness in the topology optimization is not stated.
readings: unit thickness in model units (e.g. 1 mm)

items.description: R = 1.2 has no units (Fig. 2 caption, Sec. 4.1). Eq. 7 uses centre-to-centre element distances, but the text does not say whether R is in element widths, cm or mm (E is given in N/mm^2). On a 1 cm mesh the first two readings coincide: only the 4 edge neighbours get weight 0.2. They differ on any other mesh.
readings: 1.2 mm in a mm-based model (smaller than one element, so effectively no filtering)

items.description: The Sec. 1.3.1 prose and the chain rule in Eqs. 8-15 describe density filtering. Eq. 6 as printed has rho_i instead of rho_j in the numerator, which literally gives rho_hat_i = rho_i (no filtering). Eq. 11 also evaluates the SIMP term with the unfiltered rho_j. So the exact filter variant is uncertain.
readings: standard density filter (rho_j in numerator; stiffness and volume use filtered densities)
sensitivity filter (Sigmund type, as in the 88-line code ft=1)

items.entity: Optimizer and update parameters for the topology optimization
items.description: The optimizer for the topology-optimization step is never named. MMA and SQP are mentioned only for frame size/layout optimization (Sec. 2.4, 4.1), and no move limit or damping is given.
readings: Optimality Criteria, move limit 0.2, damping exponent 0.5

items.description: Only 'Maximum iterations = 200' is given (Fig. 2 caption, Sec. 4.1). There is no tolerance on density or compliance change for this step; the 1e-4 tolerances in Table 1 apply to frame optimization only.
readings: stop when max |delta rho| < 0.01, else at 200 iterations
stop when relative compliance change < 1e-4, else at 200 iterations

items.description: No starting design is given for the SIMP run (Sec. 1.3.1, 2.1).

Sec. 2.1 mentions no passive regions. Sec. 4.1 says 'Fixed-end boundary pixels and force-applied pixels were tagged so no alteration is allowed during any stages of optimization'. It is unclear whether these elements were held solid during topology optimization or only protected during skeletonization and frame optimization.
readings: no passive elements in the topology optimization
loaded element(s) at the load point held solid (rho = 1)
loaded element(s) plus the element column along the clamped edge held solid

items.entity: How the point load is applied on the mesh
items.description: Sec. 2.1/4.1 call it a point load 18 cm below the top edge, but Sec. 4.1 and the Fig. 4/18 captions refer to the 'loaded element pixel' or 'force-applied pixels'. It is unclear whether the force goes on one node or is shared by the nodes of one boundary element (and by the through-thickness nodes if hexahedra are used).
readings: single nodal force at the right-edge node 18 cm below the top (node row 18 of 0-52 on a 1 cm mesh)
force split equally between the two right-edge nodes of the element spanning 18-19 cm below the top
force split equally between the two right-edge nodes of the element spanning 17-18 cm below the top
